layers.label: U.S. House
layers.rank_note: 28 congressional districts — the largest districts Florida carries below the state itself, larger on average than its 40 Senate districts

source.answers: The U.S. House district covering the point, and the representative holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 4 (119th Congressional Districts), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 28 features for Florida, measured 2026-11-11. These are the districts the current members were elected from in 2024. TIGERweb's layer 0 carries the map for the 120th Congress, whose members were elected on 3 November 2026 and take office on 3 January 2027; measured that day, 21 of the 28 districts differ between the two maps, and the builder refuses to write layer 4 on or after that date. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: congress-roster.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the public-domain unitedstates/congress-legislators dataset — including each member's district office and Washington office.

layers.label: Florida Senate District
layers.rank_note: 40 Senate districts — smaller on average than a congressional district

source.answers: The Florida Senate district covering the point, and the senator holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 1 (2026 State Legislative Districts - Upper), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 40 features, measured 2026-11-11. Florida's Senate districts are not built from its House districts, so each chamber's map is simplified on its own. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: fl-senate-members.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the Senate's own site (flsenate.gov): the senator's name and party from the Senate's member list and each senator's own page, the senator's own e-mail address as that page prints it, and the Tallahassee office address and telephone printed there. A seat the Senate lists as vacant says so.

layers.label: County
layers.rank_note: 67 counties, pre-built from TIGERweb; the instance's offline anchor layer, larger on average than a House district

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — State_County, layer 1, pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 67 features, measured 2026-11-11. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET. Each Florida county is governed by an elected board of county commissioners, unless its charter sets up another government (Miami-Dade's commission and mayor; Duval's government is consolidated with the City of Jacksonville's), and elects officers such as a sheriff, a clerk of the circuit court, a property appraiser, a tax collector and a supervisor of elections; no list of them was read in this pass, so the card names the county only. Recorded as gap fl-county-officials.

layers.label: School District
layers.rank_note: 67 school districts, one for each county and the same ground, drawn from a tile archive mirrored from TIGERweb

source.answers: The public school district covering the point.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — School, layer 0 (unified school districts), mirrored into a vector-tile archive this site serves (scripts/mirror_tiger_tiles.py); 67 features for Florida, measured 2026-11-11, one for each county, as Florida's constitution makes each county a school district. TIGERweb's secondary and elementary layers carry nothing for Florida, so they are not drawn.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET. Each school district elects a school board, and no list of the members was read in this pass — recorded as gap fl-school-board-members.

layers.label: Florida House District
layers.rank_note: 120 House districts — about three in each Senate district, though no rule nests them, and smaller on average than a county

source.answers: The Florida House district covering the point, and the member holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 2 (2026 State Legislative Districts - Lower), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 120 features, measured 2026-11-11. Simplified on its own, by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval, and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: fl-house-members.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the House's own site (flhouse.gov): the member's name and party from the House's member list, and the Capitol office address and telephone from each member's contact page. The House links an e-mail form for each member rather than printing an address, so none is shown. A seat the House lists as vacant says so.

layers.label: ZIP Code
layers.rank_note: 1,013 ZIP Code Tabulation Areas inside Florida (1,102 in the app's bounding box), drawn from a tile archive of the ones inside the state; the layer hides outside it

source.answers: The ZIP Code Tabulation Area covering the point — the Census Bureau's areal approximation of the USPS delivery routes sharing a ZIP code, not a postal boundary.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, layer 11 of the PUMA/TAD/TAZ/UGA/ZCTA service, mirrored into a vector-tile archive of the ZCTAs inside Florida (scripts/mirror_tiger_tiles.py). ZCTAs carry NO STATE FIELD because they cross state lines, so this is the one TIGERweb layer here fetched by a bounding ENVELOPE rather than STATE='12'. 1,102 features in the app's box, which reaches into Alabama and Georgia, 1,013 of them inside Florida and kept in the archive, measured 2026-11-11.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a ZIP code is a mail-routing convenience, not a unit of government, so nobody is elected from one. The card says what the boundary actually is rather than leaving a reader to assume it means more.
source.applies: Florida. The layer is hidden outside the state outline, because outside it the Census's point query answers with a neighbouring state's real ZIP code.

layers.label: City, Town or Village
layers.rank_note: 411 incorporated cities, towns and villages, drawn from a tile archive mirrored from TIGERweb

source.answers: The incorporated city, town or village containing the point, or that the point is outside every one.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Places_CouSub_ConCity_SubMCD, layer 4 (incorporated places), mirrored into a vector-tile archive this site serves (scripts/mirror_tiger_tiles.py); 411 features for Florida, measured 2026-11-11: 267 cities, 123 towns and 21 villages, every one an active government. MOST OF FLORIDA IS IN NO CITY, TOWN OR VILLAGE (10.3% of its land, 14,353.0 of 138,974.0 km2, is inside one), and there the county is the general-purpose local government, so an empty card says the point is outside every one rather than naming a place. The Census's census-designated places and county subdivisions are statistical areas with no government and are not drawn.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET. No statewide roster of Florida's mayors and council members was read in this pass; the card names the place and links nothing it has not verified. Recorded as gap fl-municipal-officeholders.

layers.label: Police Station
layers.rank_note: nearest police stations by straight-line distance — a point layer, ranked with the other nearest-N layers

source.answers: The three nearest police stations to the point, by straight-line distance, with each one's address.

boundary.label: USGS The National Map — structures layer 53 (Police Stations), queried live at runtime by a bounding envelope through the paged loader. Public domain. Measured 2026-11-11: 678 points in Florida's envelope, under the service's 2,000-record cap, and paged anyway so that stops being a fact anyone has to re-check.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a police station is a facility, not an elected district. Nobody is elected from one.
source.applies: Florida — plus the border strip its envelope necessarily includes. A BUILDING, NOT A JURISDICTION: which agency answers at a given point is a service-area question this instance has not been researched for, so the card says where the nearest are and never who serves you. Nearest-three is a proximity fact, so for a reader near the state line the nearest one really may be in a neighbouring state, and the card's intro says these are straight-line distances.

anchor_point.note: Florida State Capitol, 400 South Monroe Street, Tallahassee, Leon County

negative_point.note: Open water in the Gulf, about 200 km west of Sarasota — outside Florida and outside every other instance in the fleet, and inside permalink_gate so the app answers the click and every shipped layer correctly returns nothing. Measured 2026-11-11: TIGERweb's state layer places it in no state and its ZCTA layer in no ZIP code (controls: the State Capitol returns Florida and ZIP code 32399, and a point in Havana returns no state), none of the state's shipped boundary files contains it, and none of the 25 outlines in fleet-outlines.json does. IT IS FAR OUT TO SEA, SO NO NEIGHBOUR'S GO-LIVE MOVES IT.

geometry.note: The whole-Florida outline for the coverage wash (loadMetroOutline), dissolved from the county fabric (67 counties).
The 67 counties — the instance's offline anchor layer and the ground the coverage tests use.
The 28 U.S. House districts, TIGERweb layer 4 (CD119), the map the sitting members were elected from in 2024, drawn until 3 January 2027.
The 40 Florida Senate districts, TIGERweb layer 1 (2026 State Legislative Districts - Upper).
The 120 Florida House districts, TIGERweb layer 2 (2026 State Legislative Districts - Lower).

The ZIP code search index (scripts/build_zip_index.mjs): one Point per ZIP code the app's ZIP layer draws, at the spot inside it on the layer's own ground farthest from every edge, with its extent and its layer, so a ZIP code typed into the search box selects that spot, turns the ZIP layer on and pins it for comparison (ENGINE geocoder-search, showZip). A ZIP code with no spot 75 m clear of every edge is left out, and one that crosses into another app's state is listed by whichever app holds more of it. GENERATED from data/app/tiles/zip-code.pmtiles, with each spot inside metro-outline.json (the outline its coverage test reads); --check rebuilds it from the committed archive and outline. Exact count, because it changes only when the Census Bureau changes its ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, and that wants reading rather than a widened bound.

The recorded gaps this instance ships with, rendered by the data-gaps panel.

The officers Florida elects statewide and its two U.S. senators: state, officers (office, name, the office's own website, the day the name was last checked there) and usSenate. Built weekly by scripts/build_statewide_officials.py from fl/data/source/statewide-officials.source.json, which lists each office, the name and the page that must print it; the build reads robots.txt before every page, refuses to write when a page it read no longer prints the name, keeps the last checked record when a page cannot be read, and takes the senators from senate.gov's own list. Network-first: a name can change.
